title: Automated scenario-based retention composer and attested evidence workflow for prompt/response/log/metric artifacts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need clear, auditable retention controls for the four primary artifact classes (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics) that can be composed into scenario presets (e.g., 'Regulated PII flow', 'GDPR minimize', 'Audit-ready full retention'). Current retention UI and APIs require manual per-route configuration and produce brittle evidence exports that are hard for legal/compliance teams to validate.

Goal: Deliver a scenario-driven Retention Composer that: (1) lets operators pick or author scenario presets which map to per-tenant/per-route retention rules across artifact classes; (2) produces tamper-evident attested evidence bundles (signed metadata + chained hashes) suitable for audits; (3) enables residency-aware retention rules (region pinning + cross-region export); and (4) provides a preview/simulator to estimate storage impact and evidence size.

Scope: UX + API for editor and presets, backend policy engine to translate scenarios into per-route TTLs and sampling rules, evidence exporter format and signer integration (KMS/HSM), residency-aware routing hooks for exports, and CI gating to ensure no scenario rollback breaks SLOs. Excludes: automatic legal approval workflows (out of scope for initial release).
acceptance_criteria: Retention Composer UI: create/edit/save scenario presets that set TTLs and sampling rates for prompts, responses, request logs, metrics
API: POST/GET endpoints for scenario presets and per-tenant binding; changes are versioned and immutable once released
Evidence Bundles: exported bundles contain signed manifest, chained SHA-256 digests for artifact shards, and a human-readable audit summary
Residency: scenario can require region pinning for stored artifacts and the system prevents cross-region exports unless explicitly authorized
Preview Simulator: shows estimated monthly storage, expected export bundle size, and sample evidence timeline for a sample traffic profile
Security: evidence signing uses customer KMS when available; fallback to Redwood attestation; security sign-off obtained
Backward Compatibility: existing per-route TTLs remain honored; binding a scenario should not silently change per-route settings without a preview and confirmation
Operational: rollout supports canary binding (10% of routes) and automatic rollback on retention-export errors
notes: Design note: composer should support both policy-first (RPEL-like) and template-first workflows — operators choose which UI path to use
Implementation idea: translate scenario presets into a small set of primitive rules (TTL, sample_rate, residency_region, export_schedule) which the runtime can enforce without expensive lookups
Evidence format: ZIP with manifest.json, artifacts/*.ndjson (sharded), chainlinks.txt (hash chain), signature.sig; manifest must include per-shard offsets and schema version
KMS integration: prefer EKM/HSM customer keys; when unavailable include a Redwood-produced attestation header and key-rotation metadata
Telemetry: emit retention-affecting config change events to audit log with actor, diff, and before/after preview
Edgecases: handling deleted/retained metrics derived from aggregated counters vs raw time-series—documented in runbook
